newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: New U.N. chief goes home to Ghana for festivities.
newsitem.headline: New U.N. chief goes home to Ghana for festivities.

text.p: Kofi Annan, the incoming U.N. secretary-general, was leaving on Thursday for his home country, Ghana, to take part in festivities to celebrate his victory in the recent U.N. elections.
He will be accompanied by his wife Nane, a Swedish artist and lawyer, and their children Ama, 26, Kojo, 23, and Nina, 25, a member of the family said.
Among his surviving family members in Ghana is his 88-year old mother, Victoria.
Annan, 58, the undersecretary-general for peacekeeping operations, was sworn in as the seventh U.N. secretary-general on Tuesday. He takes office on Jan. 1, succeeding Boutros Boutros-Ghali of Egypt.
He is the first secretary-general from sub-Saharan Africa and the first to have risen through the ranks of the U.N. bureaucracy.
